evidence.title: Giftig lek op vrachtschip in Waaslandhaven: strafonderzoek geopend (VRT NWS, 14 Jul 22:53, updated 15 Jul 16:45)
evidence.excerpt: A hole of about 10x10 cm developed in a hydrogen fluoride tank container aboard MSC Mia Summer II during loading at Deurganck Dock, possibly via a twistlock; the substance evaporated completely. 186 people medically evaluated; two still in hospital, one in intensive care. The Ghent labour prosecutor opened a criminal investigation; maritime police and the labour inspectorate are examining workplace-safety compliance. Port authority: all port activities can resume.
evidence.note: cause, casualties, investigation; shipper not named

evidence.title: Toxic spill shuts down two container terminals at Port of Antwerp (Maritime Executive, 15 Jul 2026)
evidence.excerpt: Traffic in nearby waterways was temporarily suspended and the port activated cordon and evacuation plans for the Kieldrecht Lock complex and all of the Deurganck Dock. 150+ potentially exposed, 28 hospitalised with serious symptoms, one in intensive care. Antwerp Gateway (DP World) reopened early Wednesday afternoon and marine traffic partially resumed; MPET remained closed. Belgian prosecutors opened a criminal inquiry. Fumes did not reach residential areas.
evidence.note: extent of closure: whole dock and lock, not part of one terminal

evidence.title: MPET partially reopens after hydrofluoric acid leak (WorldCargo News, 16 Jul 2026)
evidence.excerpt: Quay 1718 resumed shipping, lorry and inland-waterway operations at 22:00 on Wednesday 15 July; DP World's Antwerp Gateway (quay 1700) also resumed. Full MPET reopening expected Friday 17 July at 14:00 pending cleaning and safety clearance. The northern side of the dock (quay 1742) stayed closed for extended decontamination; the front office was not yet cleared. The leaking container was removed Wednesday morning. 186 assessed; 25 in hospital; one in stable intensive care.

evidence.title: MPET STS cranes heavily damaged after toxic cloud incident (WorldCargo News, 24 Jul 2026; paywalled, lead only)
evidence.excerpt: Ten days on, the berth at quay 1742 is out of operation; around 90 employees' vehicles were declared a total loss; three ship-to-shore cranes were damaged by the acid cloud (windows, possibly cabling) and may need to be partially replaced. Rail operations at MPET resumed Monday 20 July at 06:00 (Flows). No reopening date for the north berth was found by 7 Sep 2026.
evidence.note: the smaller node stayed shut: berth 1742 out for weeks, not days

evidence.title: Drewry World Container Index, 16 July 2026
evidence.excerpt: WCI fell 2% to USD 4,547/40ft; Shanghai-Rotterdam -1% to USD 4,873; Shanghai-Genoa -3%. Drivers named: capacity management, blank sailings, geopolitical disruptions (US-Iran, Bab el-Mandeb, possible Hormuz security charges). Congestion at European ports is easing, with a 33-hour week-on-week fall in average waiting time at Genoa. Antwerp, Deurganck and the leak are not mentioned.

evidence.title: Toxic leak deepens congestion at Europe's second-busiest port (Sourcing Journal, ~16 Jul 2026; paywalled, headline only)
evidence.excerpt: Headline attributes deepened congestion at Antwerp-Bruges to the leak. Body not retrievable (402). Kuehne+Nagel's 15-21 July port update gives no waiting-time metric for Antwerp and says all port and vessel activities returned to normal on 17 July; it lists waiting times at Rotterdam (1.71 days), Bremerhaven (1 day), Hamburg (1.24 days), Genoa (1.2 days), Fos (2 days) and Barcelona (2.25 days).
evidence.note: congestion commentary cited the leak; the falsifier of the indices call names commentary as well as indices

evidence.title: MSC halts MPET operations after toxic gas leak (Kuehne+Nagel port update, 15-16 Jul 2026) and forwarder notes
evidence.excerpt: The carrier's advisory listed Quay 1700, Quay 1718, Quay 1742 and Medrep S11 as affected and said the incident had significantly impacted terminal activities; vessels moored between berth 1730 and the dock entrance were allowed to leave on 15 July. A forwarder wrote that some vessels had likely bypassed Antwerp for Zeebrugge or Rotterdam (an expectation, not a reported omission). No carrier omission or rerouting notice citing the leak was found; Hapag-Lloyd's week-29 update was unreachable.
evidence.note: carrier schedules: operational advisory, no omissions found; coverage thin on carrier notices

evidence.title: Exceptional disruption reduces throughput at Antwerp-Bruges (Kuehne+Nagel on the port's H1 2026 report)
evidence.excerpt: H1 2026: 133.9m tonnes, down 2.4%. Estimated losses: March maritime-chain strike 100,000 TEU; April oil spill 85,000 TEU; June pilot action about 85,000 TEU. Imports from the Middle East Gulf down 57%; weak western European exports. The July leak is not in the H1 figures.
evidence.note: node recurrence: three disruptions in four months before this one

resolutions.scorer_note: Second clean round; self-scored, second scorer to follow (B2). Map: tank container on a vessel at the MSC/PSA terminal, contained within a day (container removed Wednesday morning), no fatalities, river not closed: all right, and the falsifier did not fire. But the scale was badly under-called: the whole dock and the Kieldrecht lock closed, Antwerp Gateway shut for a day, 186 people assessed, 28 hospitalised, ~90 vehicles written off, three cranes damaged. A hit on the falsifier's terms; a poor map.

The dock as such was not closed beyond 3 days (Antwerp Gateway 1 day; MPET declared safe 17 Jul 14:00), so the falsifier did not fire, but the claim 'fully operational within 3 days' is false: rail resumed 20 Jul and the north berth (quay 1742) was still out with three damaged cranes ten days later, no reopening date found. The rule I cited says exactly this (duration lives one node smaller); I cited it and still called the headline node. Misread: mechanism right, operator wrong. Baseline (port shut for a week) also wrong.

Prices held: WCI fell 2% on 16 Jul with European congestion easing and no Antwerp mention; K+N reports normal operations from 17 Jul. But my falsifier named congestion commentary as well as indices, and a Sourcing Journal headline attributed deepened congestion to the leak (body paywalled). Falsifier fired on narrative. The pricing mechanism (recurring disruption priced as weather) was right; the call's scope was the error. Misread. Coverage thin: the commentary body could not be read. Baseline (rates up) wrong.

MSC issued an operational advisory naming the affected quays; vessels held in the dock were released on 15 Jul. No carrier omission or rerouting notice citing the leak was found within 7 days; a forwarder's note that vessels 'likely' bypassed to Zeebrugge or Rotterdam is an expectation, not a notice. Carrier notices were thinly covered (Hapag-Lloyd's page unreachable), so the second scorer should weigh this one.

Ordering held: physical (dock 1-3 days, north berth weeks, cranes) > terminal throughput > carrier schedules (delays and an advisory, no omissions) > indices (nil) > equity (nil). I had called carrier schedules nil; they were small, not nil, but still below throughput. Baseline (everything moves on the day) wrong.

Null hit, weight 0.2. No listed party's move in the three sessions after 14 Jul was attributed to the leak; Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd moved on the Hormuz blockade reinstated the same day. Baseline (shipping stocks down): unverifiable against that tide.
Null hit, weight 0.2. MSC, PSA and DP World are private; Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd hold small positions; every holder on the node is sign minus. Time-bounded falsifier did not fire.

No order restricting dangerous-goods handling citing the incident was found within 30 days (English and Dutch). A criminal investigation by the Ghent labour prosecutor is open with no party named; the liability half of the claim is therefore unverified rather than confirmed, and I do not credit the liability-periphery rule with an outcome it has not yet produced: mechanism unknown.
No force majeure, allocation or supply notice citing the leak was found within 14 days. No-mechanism call by declaration.
